cards.a: SD-Access is Cisco's intent-based campus fabric: a VXLAN overlay (data plane) with a LISP control plane and ISE policy, orchestrated by DNA Center. It delivers macro/micro segmentation, host mobility, and policy-driven access across the wired and wireless campus.

cards.q: What are the three planes of SD-Access and their technologies?
cards.a: Control plane = LISP, data plane = VXLAN, and policy = ISE with SGT. In short: LISP routes, VXLAN tunnels, ISE decides access.

cards.q: What are the main fabric roles in SD-Access?
cards.a: Fabric edge (access switch = entry point), border (exit to outside/legacy networks), control plane node (LISP map server = mapping), and fabric WLC (wireless). Edge = entry, border = exit, control = mapping.

cards.q: What is the difference between macro and micro segmentation in SD-Access?
cards.a: Macro segmentation separates networks using a Virtual Network (VN) built on a VRF carried by VXLAN; micro segmentation separates security groups inside those networks using ISE/SGT. Macro = separate networks, micro = security groups within them.

cards.q: Why does SD-Access keep host IPs stable during roaming?
cards.a: Because policy is group-based and follows the security group, not the VLAN, so hosts keep their IP addresses while roaming anywhere in the fabric.

cards.q: What are the key components of the SD-Access stack and their jobs?
cards.a: VXLAN (data plane tunnels), LISP (EID to RLOC mapping), ISE (AAA + SGT), and DNA Center (orchestration). Together they form the SD-Access stack.

cards.q: Which commands verify SD-Access LISP, VXLAN, and host tracking?
cards.a: show lisp session, show lisp map-cache, show vxlan vni, show vlan vn-segment, show ip device tracking, and show authentication sessions.

cards.q: How do you troubleshoot roaming, VXLAN, and policy failures in SD-Access?
cards.a: If a host can't roam, check LISP with show lisp map-cache; if VXLAN is down, verify the VNI with show vxlan vni; wrong policy points to ISE/SGT (check authentication sessions); fabric down points to DNA Center; and lost segmentation means the macro/micro mapping (vlan vn-segment) is misconfigured.

cards.q: Which protocol is the SD-Access data plane and which is the control plane?
cards.a: A common mix-up: VXLAN is the data plane, LISP is the control plane, and ISE/SGT handles policy. DNA Center orchestrates all three.

cards.q: How does SD-Access enforce policy on groups rather than VLANs?
cards.a: ISE assigns Security Group Tags (SGTs) used for micro segmentation, so policy is group-based and follows the SGT rather than being tied to a VLAN.
